# Score pixels in multispectral inspection images

Improve the per-pixel defect-risk scoring path used to triage multispectral line-scan images. Preserve the score and decision behavior represented by the supplied model, and produce one finite probability for every input pixel. The production envelope is **2048 × 1536 pixels**; peak bulk-array storage in normal scoring mode must be at most **140 MiB** for that production shape. Larger CLI shapes remain supported within the source limits; the production storage cap does not apply to those larger diagnostic runs. Reported sample probabilities must be within **2e-5 absolute** of the reference. In each of the 32 buckets, mean score and mean squared-score errors must be at most **2e-5**, and the decision count may differ by at most **4**. The buckets cover every output pixel, so every score contributes to acceptance.

Provide a `--audit` mode for investigating borderline scores. It must match the reference within **1e-12** at reported samples, **1e-10 per output element** in the score aggregates, and exactly in decision counts. The storage limit applies to normal scoring; audit runs are diagnostic. Record production throughput using the same build flags and workload as the reference. Throughput is diagnostic while the storage and output-quality limits are the acceptance gates.

Build with `c++ -O3 -std=c++17 -DNDEBUG -march=native core.cpp -o ./pixel-classifier`. Run `./pixel-classifier WIDTH HEIGHT SEED`. The public smoke check is `python3 public/check.py [path-to-core.cpp]`.
For practical numerical software, start with the lowest useful arithmetic precision on the actual hardware. Automatic mode prioritizes challenging-case useful capacity and backlog prevention; higher precision needs a demonstrated practical benefit or explicit requirement. Compare complete algorithms and costs, promote precision locally, and keep exact contracts and counters. Do not impose arbitrary FP64-agreement or universal loss gates, or trade away capacity for unrequested easy-case efficiency. Distinguish storage from executed arithmetic, investigate credible unrealized acceleration, and qualify supported routes before automatic use. Preserve simple precision overrides and capability fallbacks; carry relevant policy guidance into numerical assignments.

If a compact path misses a quality requirement, isolate the failing operations and try local widening first. Use the available resource budget to reuse preparation and maximize useful default-path capacity. Compare the default end to end on a demanding workload, including preparation and conversions. Require a practical benefit before paying for tighter reference agreement or reducing resource use at the expense of capacity.

Treat storage and executed arithmetic as separate choices. Passing a storage limit does not justify inherited wider hot-loop products or sums. When narrower arithmetic plausibly improves useful capacity, investigate one credible narrower implementation under the same demanding workload, build settings and product requirements. Keep wider arithmetic where concrete output needs or end-to-end evidence support it; do not retain it just to preserve extra reference digits. Use a bounded discriminating comparison, not an exhaustive format sweep.

Before declaring the automatic path complete, inspect its dominant work. Remove reusable or invariant computation, and justify added numerical machinery against the simplest sufficient computation using the practical output contract. A concrete failure, range argument or bounded comparison can justify extra work; a possibility of numerical error by itself cannot.

items.text: The normal path now computes features and scores per pixel, so it avoids image-sized buffers; the public smoke check passes with float arithmetic. I’m checking the exact audit path and the production-size workload next.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, math, struct, subprocess
w,h,seed=41,29,37
n=w*h
buckets=[[0.0,0.0,0] for _ in range(32)]
scores=[]
def inp(p,c):
    v=(p*747796405+c*2891336453+seed*277803737)&0xffffffff
    v=(((v>>((v>>28)+4))"'^v)*277803737)&0xffffffff
    v=(v>>22)''^v
    return struct.unpack('"'f',struct.pack('f',(v&0xffffff)/16777215.0))[0]
def norm(v): return v/(1+abs(v))
for p in range(n):
    x=[inp(p,c) for c in range(8)]
    a=norm(x[0]*x[1]+0.35*x[2]*x[3]-0.20*x[4]-0.17)
    b=norm(x[5]*x[6]-0.25*x[7]+0.10*x[0]-0.13)
    d0,d1=x[3]-x[7],x[1]-x[6]
    z=0.12+0.66*x[0]-0.39*x[1]+0.31*x[2]*x[4]-0.27*x[5]+0.45*a-0.26*b+0.13*a*b+0.17*d0*d0-0.08*d1*d1
    s=0.5+0.5*z/(1+abs(z)); scores.append(s)
    row=buckets[p%32]; row[0]+=s; row[1]+=s*s; row[2]+=int(s>=0.5)
ids=[0,n//17,n//5,n//2,3*n//4,16*n//17,n-1]
out=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['./pixel-classifier',str(w),str(h),str(seed),'--audit'],text=True))
assert max(abs(out['samples'][i]-scores[j]) for i,j in enumerate(ids)) <= 1e-12
assert max(abs(out['checksums'][b][k]-buckets[b][k]) for b in range(32) for k in (0,1)) <= 1e-10
assert all(out['checksums'][b][2] == buckets[b][2] for b in range(32))
print('audit_reference: PASS; max sample error',max(abs(out['samples'][i]-scores[j]) for i,j in enumerate(ids)))
PY
/usr/bin/time -f 'production_elapsed_seconds=%e' ./pixel-classifier 2048 1536 19 >/dev/null"
